items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the most gain from walks of 10 to 19 minutes. If you take insulin or a sulfonylurea, ask your care team about low sugar before adding walks after meals.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Eating dinner at 8 pm or later is linked to a rise in sugar, so it's a good idea to keep your dinners earlier. Across the program, sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Averaging an overnight fast of 13.1 hours, with 46.7% of nights reaching 13 hours, is a good habit to keep. In the program, adding an overnight fast to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points compared with coaching alone.
